reason: Grouping fibres seems like the first step toward building a muscle that can move the arm.
expectation: I expect a bundle or group of muscle fibres, though it may still need connective tissue.

alternatives.reason: Attaching the triceps also advances the goal, but I want to build the other muscle first.

effect: The fibres formed a bundle, so adding connective tissue looks like the next step in building a muscle.
reaction: The paired poses help connect the individual fibre to the larger bundle.
reason: The sheaths appear to organize and support the bundle as a muscle.
expectation: I expect a wrapped muscle bundle, possibly forming part of a complete muscle.

alternatives.reason: Attaching the triceps would advance the arm assembly, but I want to finish building this muscle first.

effect: The bundle and sheaths formed a biceps with tendons, showing how the fibres’ pull reaches bone.
reaction: The explanation that muscle pulls but cannot push makes the need for an opposing muscle clearer.
reason: I want to attach the biceps I just built to the arm skeleton.
expectation: I expect the biceps tendons to attach to the skeleton, leaving the triceps to be added.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attaching, but I chose to continue with the biceps first.

effect: The biceps is attached and shown bending the elbow; the remaining extensor slot points to the triceps.
reaction: The two poses make the biceps’ pull clear.
reason: I’ll add the triceps to fill the extensor slot and complete the opposing pair.
expectation: I expect the triceps to attach across the elbow and provide a pull in the opposite direction.

effect: The triceps completes the opposing pair, showing how coordinated muscle activity bends and straightens the elbow.
reaction: The opposing pulls make the arm’s movement clearer.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and should supply the arm’s tissues.
expectation: I expect a supplied arm assembly, with vessels reaching its muscles and other tissues.

effect: The vessels completed the arm and connected the muscles’ cellular energy needs to a larger circulation that has yet to be built.
reaction: The link back to ATP-making machinery was useful, though the vessel addition felt predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the triceps was most worthwhile because its opposing pull explained how the elbow can both bend and straighten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grouping the fibres was straightforward but contributed less explanation on its own than the later construction steps.

surprise.text: The connective tissue sheaths formed a complete biceps with tendons; the explanation clarified how the fibres’ pull reaches bone.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary. Adding blood vessels had a clear purpose, although it was the only offered combination.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the unfinished vessel connections become part of a larger circulation, especially after seeing how the arm’s tissues depend on cellular energy.
